steps.text: Place vegetable oil, ranch dressing mix, crushed red pepper flakes, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper in a 2-gallon resealable plastic bag.
Seal the bag and squeeze with your hands until oil and spices are well combined.
Place crackers into the bag, seal, and turn the bag over to coat crackers with spice mix.
Let sit for about 1 hour, then turn again. Repeat several times until crackers are well coated with spice mix, then let the bag sit for 8 hours to overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Alabama Fire Crackers
raw_recipe.description: Fire crackers are easy to make with saltine crackers, garlic, onion, black pepper, and plenty of red chili flakes for a fiery hot, savory snack.

video.description: These spicy crackers are perfect for your next snack spread! Make these for your friends as holiday gifts or game day treats!

review.reviewBody: I made a version similar to this yesterday with ranch and oyster crackers & when I read the reviews for this, I read one where the reviewer had been using a packet of italian seasoning instead of ranch by accident. I love ranch dressing, but sometimes ranch seasoning packets don't taste quite right without being mixed in sour cream, buttermilk or something in my opinion so I made these today w/ italian seasoning in place of ranch seasoning & they were AMAZING. I don't normally give 5 stars if I change something in a recipe but these were too good to give any less than 5 stars. I cut back the oil to 1/2 a cup (only because I couldn't justify the calories for the full amount and these are so good I could eat every single cracker!) and used two packages of saltines and that was perfect for me. I will make these all the time, thanks for sharing your recipe!!

I made two adjustments for these. I used Peanut Oil,but a little less of it and after letting it soak overnight I lined them all off on a cookie sheet with paper towels underneath. I then place them in the oven on the warm setting. That does two things, 1)the heat helps cook the spices on to the cracker, 2) the heat and paper towels help push out and absorb the excess oil making them not quite as oily.

I make the same recipe.. I use oyster crackers. I put them in a big bowl and have my husband shake them up every 15 minutes for 2 hours. Then I set them in the refrigerator. They don’t get a chance to go 9 hours. My husband is chowing them down as soon as he can.

I made 4 batches of these for a family party and they were gone within an hour. I did make one change: I baked the crackers at 325 when they were done marinating overnight. I was worried they'd be too greasy but honestly I think they would have been fine as-is. I also made half of them extra spicy by adding cayenne and ghost pepper sauce to the marinade mix. I wouldn't touch them personally, but hotter = better for my in-laws. Anyway, huge hit and I plan to make more tomorrow. P.S. I thought the recipe called for regular saltines, but this was about a year ago so I'm not sure if the multi-grain is an update or if I just goofed. I think either would be fine!
Great snack. I used 1 1/2cups butter,melted and added 1 Tbs. Italian seasoning, I also substituted 2 boxes of Club minis. Baked for 30 minutes @ 250°, stirring halfway through.
Addictive. I used half ranch dressing and Italian and cut back to 1 1/3 olive oil. . I also put in oven on cookie sheet for 30 minutes at 225.

I make a very similar recipe. But I cut the oil substantially. Like in half. And for oil, I used half olive oil and half salad oil. My recipe also called for baking on a sheet pan at 250 degrees, tossing occasionally, but do not let the crackers toast. I also tossed the crackers in a large Tupperware style container rather than a disposable plastic bag, stirring every few hours.

I used regular saltines, divided the crackers and ingredients evenly into two 2 quart bags, with the exception of using the Fiesta blend ranch mix in one of the bags. The Fiesta blend kicked up the flavor quite nicely. Was a hit with the family.

I used less red pepper flakes - half as much - and it was plenty hot enough. I've also discovered that switching out the red pepper flakes for 4 chicken bouillon cubes makes a homemade Ranch Chicken in a Biscuit cracker that is even more popular than the Firecrackers.

I didn't have enough saltine crackers so I used a mix of triscuits, oyster crackers, butter crackers, and a couple other varieties. I used one packet of each ranch and Italian and kept the rest of the ingredients to recipe. I will be making this again. Yummy

This is a fantastic recipe. I make this every year for the holidays. Actually getting ready to make it in a few minutes to take to work tomorrow. It’s always a big hit. I have tweaked the recipe for my tastes. I used 2 italian dressing packets, 1/2 cup oil and 1 tablespoon of red pepper flakes. Everything else I left the same. These crackers go great with cheese balls. I usually make the dried beef cheese balls.
I make it at least twice a month
OMG this is delicious - will be a staple for us - crackers have some heat without being too hot - amazing with pimento cheese

I made it exactly the way the recipe reads, and this was amazing and no, they are not oily. They are not wet. They are not greasy. They are crispy and flavorful. Even my vegan daughter had to sneak a bite even though the ranch dip seasoning wasn’t vegan and she and her husband LOVED them!!! They held up nice in storage sealed in a container. They remained crispy. They did not get stale and they are rich so you don’t eat too many of them.
So easy and they are my families favorite. I followed the directions and they turned out perfect.
they were awesome just a little oily for my taste. I will make them again but with less oil
I baked mine at 250 for 10 minutes uses rhey are delicious.
Used avocado oil based on her YouTube vid, & really old red pepper flakes. These were Great! Have to try with fresher red pepper.
Great floating in some homemade chicken noodle soup! My husband (& I) love the spicy/mild contrast.
Everyone loved these. I did modify it by using only a scant cup of canola oil and 2 Tbsp of red pepper flakes.
